subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted external workspace agent-config discovery, or keep registration explicit and prioritize zero-restart explicit agent management?
rationale: The request adds a config option, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, precedence rules, and live routing/session semantics that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep explicit registration
options.body: Continue using central config, `$include`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and solve the reported pain through hot-load/hot-remove explicit registration before adding glob discovery.

options.title: Design trusted discovery
options.body: Approve a core discovery contract only after defining trusted roots, glob bounds, realpath/symlink behavior, validation, precedence, reload semantics, and security proof.

options.title: Reject core discovery
options.body: Keep workspace scanning outside core as operator tooling or plugin/ClawHub work unless a smaller missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit registration
recommendation.body: Continue using central config, `$include`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and solve the reported pain through hot-load/hot-remove explicit registration before adding glob discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the user-visible `agents.list`/agent picker surface is Peter's commit, and that is the surface maintainers must decide whether discovery should extend.
